action: Maersk customers and partners: watch for company updates on what data was involved, be alert to invoices or shipping messages that look unusual, and verify any payment-detail change by phone.
exec: Maersk disclosed data theft from a system inherited through an acquisition; it says findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed.
plain: Shipping company Maersk confirmed that an intruder took data from systems of a company it acquired. A criminal group called WhiteArmor demanded $5 million; Danish outlet Ingeniøren reports the group has now published the data.

sources.name: Ingeniøren (Danish, paywalled), 13 Nov: WhiteArmor leaks the data

summary: Maersk said an intruder breached a legacy system inherited through an earlier acquisition and stole data; its advisory says the incident is isolated to a local system and findings so far strongly suggest no sensitive data has been disclosed. The WhiteArmor group claimed about 100GB (unverified) and demanded $5 million. Ingeniøren reported on 13 November that WhiteArmor had leaked all the data early.
title: Maersk confirms data theft; WhiteArmor demands $5 million

validation.note: BleepingComputer and Computing (read) both relay Maersk's customer advisory of 11 Nov. Maersk has not named the acquired company or confirmed WhiteArmor. Computing reports a WhiteArmor deadline of 7 December. Ingeniøren (read 21 Nov, paywalled, truncated) says WhiteArmor leaked the data on Thursday evening instead of 7 December; contents not readable; the publication is single-source.

review.note: date/time: occurred_at was BleepingComputer's publication time; removed. 100GB, 5M USD, strongly-suggest wording match BleepingComputer and Computing.
